about.text: A soft, crumbly cow's-milk cheese from central Asturias, set slowly by lactic acid and drained in moulds or cloth. It is eaten fresh or ripened for weeks, white or kneaded with paprika to a red-orange paste. Protected designation of origin.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.
Asturias PDO (since 2008); Wikipedia says ageing from about a week to several months (soft, semi-cured, cured), max is approximate; often with paprika (roxu)

facts.v: Atroncau (truncated cone) and trapu (squash-shaped, in cloth, drained a further 24 h), each white (blancu) or with paprika (roxu, about 1 % optional in trapu)
Curd is unmoulded, paprika kneaded in by hand or machine, then re-moulded, giving red-orange paste
